ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the side length of rhombus $ABCD$ is $2$, $\angle A=60^\circ$, point $G$ is the midpoint of $AB$, a rhombus $BEFG$ is constructed with $BG$ as its side, where point $E$ is on the extension line of $CB$, and point $P$ is the midpoint of $FD$. What is the length of $PB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect BF and BD, \\
$\because$ the side length of the rhombus ABCD is 2,\\
$\therefore$ AB = BC = CD = 2,\\
$\because$ $\angle$A = $60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$BCD is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ BD = BC = 2, $\angle$DBC = $60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DBA = $60^\circ$,\\
$\because$ point G is the midpoint of AB,\\
$\therefore$ the side length of rhombus BEFG is 1,\\
that is, BE = EF = BG = 1,\\
$\because$ point E is on the extension line of CB, $\angle$GBE = $60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$FBG = $30^\circ$,\\
connect EG,\\
$\therefore$ EG $\perp$ FB at point O,\\
$\therefore$ OB = $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ FB = $\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\because$ $\angle$DBF = $\angle$DBA + $\angle$FBG = $90^\circ$,\\
according to the Pythagorean theorem, we get\\
DF = $\sqrt{DB^2 + BF^2} = \sqrt{7}$,\\
$\because$ point P is the midpoint of FD,\\
$\therefore$ PB = $\frac{1}{2}$DF = $\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the figure: In the figure, the large quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and D is at the upper right; point G is located on AB; on the left side, using BG as one side, the small rhombus BEFG is constructed, E is to the lower left of B and is located on the extension of CB, and F is to the left of G; point P is marked on FD, and the problem statement says that P is the midpoint of FD. In the figure, BD and BF can also be connected and used. Then reason: The side length of rhombus ABCD is 2, so AB=BC=CD=DA=2. Because ∠A=60°, and opposite angles of a rhombus are equal, ∠C=60°. In triangle BCD, BC=CD=2, and the included angle ∠BCD=60°, therefore △BCD is an equilateral triangle, so BD=2, and ∠DBC=60°. Since AB and CB form the interior angle 120° of the rhombus at point B, therefore ∠DBA=120°-60°=60°. G is the midpoint of AB, so BG=1. The small rhombus BEFG uses BG as a side, therefore BE=EF=FG=BG=1. Also because E is on the extension of CB, and the angle relationship between AB and CB gives ∠GBE=60°. In rhombus BEFG, the diagonal BF of the small rhombus corresponding to BD bisects ∠GBE, so ∠FBG=30°. The side length of the rhombus is 1 and the included angle is 60°, so its diagonal BF=2·1·cos30°=√3. Thus ∠DBF=∠DBA+∠FBG=60°+30°=90°, so △DBF is a right triangle. By the Pythagorean theorem, DF=√(DB²+BF²)=√(2²+(√3)²)=√7. Because P is the midpoint of the hypotenuse FD of right triangle DBF, the midpoint of the hypotenuse is equidistant from the three vertices, PB=DF/2=√7/2.

method.method_draft: Synthetic angle-and-right-triangle route. First read the diagram: ABCD is the large rhombus with A upper left, B lower left, C lower right, D upper right; G lies on AB; E lies to the left of B on the same line as CB; BEFG is the smaller rhombus attached on side BG; F is left of G; P is marked on FD. From the text, AB=BC=CD=DA=2, angle A=60°, G is midpoint of AB, BEFG is a rhombus with side BG, and P is midpoint of FD. Since opposite angles in a rhombus are equal and adjacent sides are equal, triangle BCD is equilateral, so BD=2 and angle DBA=60°. Because G is midpoint of AB, BG=1, hence each side of rhombus BEFG is 1. Since E is on the extension of CB, angle GBE=60°. In rhombus BEFG, diagonal BF bisects angle GBE, so angle FBG=30°, and the long diagonal length is BF=2·1·cos30°=sqrt(3). Thus angle DBF=angle DBA+angle FBG=90°. Apply Pythagoras in right triangle DBF: DF=sqrt(2^2+(sqrt3)^2)=sqrt7. Since P is the midpoint of the hypotenuse FD of right triangle DBF, PB=DF/2=sqrt7/2.

再推理：菱形 ABCD 的边长为 2，所以 AB=BC=CD=DA=2。因为 ∠A=60°，菱形对角相等，所以 ∠C=60°。在三角形 BCD 中，BC=CD=2，且夹角 ∠BCD=60°，因此 △BCD 是等边三角形，所以 BD=2，且 ∠DBC=60°。由于 AB 与 CB 在点 B 处成菱形内角 120°，故 ∠DBA=120°-60°=60°。

G 是 AB 的中点，所以 BG=1。小菱形 BEFG 以 BG 为边，因此 BE=EF=FG=BG=1。又因为 E 在 CB 的延长线上，且 AB 与 CB 的夹角关系给出 ∠GBE=60°。在菱形 BEFG 中，BD 对应的小菱形对角线 BF 平分 ∠GBE，所以 ∠FBG=30°。菱形边长为 1，夹角为 60°，其对角线 BF=2·1·cos30°=√3。

于是 ∠DBF=∠DBA+∠FBG=60°+30°=90°，所以 △DBF 是直角三角形。由勾股定理，DF=√(DB²+BF²)=√(2²+(√3)²)=√7。因为 P 是直角三角形 DBF 的斜边 FD 的中点，所以斜边中点到三个顶点距离相等，PB=DF/2=√7/2。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the side length of rhombus $ABCD$ is $2$, $\angle A=60^\circ$, point $G$ is the midpoint of $AB$, a rhombus $BEFG$ is constructed with $BG$ as its side, where point $E$ is on the extension line of $CB$, and point $P$ is the midpoint of $FD$. What is the length of $PB$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect BF and BD, \\
$\because$ the side length of the rhombus ABCD is 2,\\
$\therefore$ AB = BC = CD = 2,\\
$\because$ $\angle$A = $60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$BCD is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ BD = BC = 2, $\angle$DBC = $60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DBA = $60^\circ$,\\
$\because$ point G is the midpoint of AB,\\
$\therefore$ the side length of rhombus BEFG is 1,\\
that is, BE = EF = BG = 1,\\
$\because$ point E is on the extension line of CB, $\angle$GBE = $60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$FBG = $30^\circ$,\\
connect EG,\\
$\therefore$ EG $\perp$ FB at point O,\\
$\therefore$ OB = $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ FB = $\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\because$ $\angle$DBF = $\angle$DBA + $\angle$FBG = $90^\circ$,\\
according to the Pythagorean theorem, we get\\
DF = $\sqrt{DB^2 + BF^2} = \sqrt{7}$,\\
$\because$ point P is the midpoint of FD,\\
$\therefore$ PB = $\frac{1}{2}$DF = $\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}}$

In the figure, BD and BF can also be connected and used.

Then reason: The side length of rhombus ABCD is 2, so AB=BC=CD=DA=2. Because ∠A=60°, and opposite angles of a rhombus are equal, ∠C=60°. In triangle BCD, BC=CD=2, and the included angle ∠BCD=60°, therefore △BCD is an equilateral triangle, so BD=2, and ∠DBC=60°. Since AB and CB form the interior angle 120° of the rhombus at point B, therefore ∠DBA=120°-60°=60°.
